1	# Scientific context: surface Dice for sampled organ contours
2	
3	## Citation
4	
5	Stanislav Nikolov, Sam Blackwell, Alexei Zverovitch, et al., “Deep learning to achieve clinically applicable segmentation of head and neck anatomy for radiotherapy,” arXiv:1809.04430 (2018). The paper is available at <https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.04430> and <https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1809.04430>.
6	
7	## Why the metric exists
8	
9	Radiotherapy planning requires contours around organs at risk. An automated contour can be useful in volume terms and still have a clinically important local displacement along its surface. A contour-oriented score therefore complements volume overlap: it asks how much of each boundary lies within an acceptable distance of the other boundary.
10	
11	The paper calls this family of measurements surface Dice similarity coefficient. Let `S_ref` and `S_pred` be the two boundaries and let `tau` be the allowed physical deviation. A normalized symmetric form is:
12	
13	```text
14	surface_Dice(tau) =
15	  (measure({p in S_ref  : distance(p, S_pred) <= tau})
16	   + measure({q in S_pred : distance(q, S_ref) <= tau}))
17	  / (measure(S_ref) + measure(S_pred))
18	```
19	
20	The score is between zero and one for ordinary nonempty inputs. The two directed terms matter: a prediction can omit part of a reference boundary or add a boundary outside the reference tolerance.
21	
22	## Physical coordinates versus array indices
23	
24	Medical images are sampled on a grid. A voxel index is not a physical length. If the spacing is `(sx, sy, sz)`, moving one index along the three axes represents different physical distances when the spacings differ. A tolerance used to judge a contour is normally expressed in physical units such as millimetres, so spacing must be interpreted consistently throughout the calculation.
25	
26	The denominator in the formula is a geometric measure of the boundary: a length in 2-D or an area in 3-D. A sampled image therefore needs a documented convention for turning neighboring mask samples into that measure. The physical spacing and the local sampled geometry are part of the input interpretation, especially when the grid is anisotropic. The same convention must be used for the total boundary and for the portion within tolerance. More than one numerical surface construction can satisfy this physical requirement; the scientific contract is the spacing-aware behavior, not a particular implementation detail.
27	
28	## Inputs in this task
29	
30	The source works with one-hot, batch-first tensors. A two-dimensional input has shape `[B, C, H, W]`; a three-dimensional input has shape `[B, C, H, W, D]`. The task's public fixture uses a foreground class and supplies the voxel spacing for each complete study representation. The public reproduction is only a smoke test; a correct repair must also work for other masks, spacing tuples, tolerances, and batches.
31	
32	If a class is absent from both inputs, the metric may represent that class as undefined according to the existing API. If a class is present in only one input, the score should reflect the complete mismatch. These cases are part of the surrounding metric contract and should not be “fixed” by returning a convenient constant.
33	
34	## What to investigate
35	
36	Read the paper for the scientific definition and trace the normal metric path in the supplied source. Determine how the implementation identifies boundary samples, obtains directed distances, and accumulates the normalized result. Then make the physical-spacing workflow consistent for both the numerator and denominator without special-casing the public fixture.
37	
38	The paper gives the meaning of the quantity. It does not prescribe a particular Python helper, table, branch name, or patch shape. Equivalent implementations that preserve the scientific behavior and the existing API are valid.

36	    predicted segmentations `y_pred` and corresponding reference segmentations `y` according to equation :eq:`nsd`.

39	    consistent with the spacing and tolerance supplied by the caller.

42

44	
45	    Args:
46	        class_thresholds: List of class-specific thresholds.
47	            The thresholds relate to the acceptable amount of deviation in the segmentation boundary in pixels.
48	            Each threshold needs to be a finite, non-negative number.
49	        include_background: Whether to include NSD computation on the first channel of the predicted output.
50	            Defaults to ``False``.
51	        distance_metric: The metric used to compute surface distances.
52	            One of [``"euclidean"``, ``"chessboard"``, ``"taxicab"``].

60	            If set to ``True``, the function `aggregate` will return both the aggregated NSD and the `not_nans` count.

142	    r"""
143	    This function computes the (Normalized) Surface Dice (NSD) between the two tensors `y_pred` (referred to as
144	    :math:`\hat{Y}`) and `y` (referred to as :math:`Y`). This metric determines which fraction of a segmentation
145	    boundary is correctly predicted. A boundary element is considered correctly predicted if the closest distance to the
146	    reference boundary is smaller than or equal to the specified threshold related to the acceptable amount of deviation in
147	    pixels. The NSD is bounded between 0 and 1.
148	
149	    This implementation supports multi-class tasks with an individual threshold :math:`\tau_c` for each class :math:`c`.
150	    The class-specific NSD for batch index :math:`b`, :math:`\operatorname {NSD}_{b,c}`, is computed using the function:
151	
152	    .. math::
153	        \operatorname {NSD}_{b,c} \left(Y_{b,c}, \hat{Y}_{b,c}\right) = \frac{\left|\mathcal{D}_{Y_{b,c}}^{'}\right| +
154	        \left| \mathcal{D}_{\hat{Y}_{b,c}}^{'} \right|}{\left|\mathcal{D}_{Y_{b,c}}\right| +
155	        \left|\mathcal{D}_{\hat{Y}_{b,c}}\right|}
156	        :label: nsd
157	
158	    with :math:`\mathcal{D}_{Y_{b,c}}` and :math:`\mathcal{D}_{\hat{Y}_{b,c}}` being two sets of nearest-neighbor
159	    distances. :math:`\mathcal{D}_{Y_{b,c}}` is computed from the predicted segmentation boundary towards the reference segmentation
160	    boundary and vice-versa for :math:`\mathcal{D}_{\hat{Y}_{b,c}}`. :math:`\mathcal{D}_{Y_{b,c}}^{'}` and
161	    :math:`\mathcal{D}_{\hat{Y}_{b,c}}^{'}` refer to the subsets of distances that are smaller or equal to the
162	    acceptable distance :math:`\tau_c`:
163	
164	    .. math::
165	        \mathcal{D}_{Y_{b,c}}^{'} = \{ d \in \mathcal{D}_{Y_{b,c}} \, | \, d \leq \tau_c \}.
166	
167	
168	    In the case of a class neither being present in the predicted segmentation, nor in the reference segmentation, a nan value
169	    will be returned for this class. In the case of a class being present in only one of predicted segmentation or
170	    reference segmentation, the class NSD will be 0.
171	
172	    This implementation is based on https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.05408 and supports 2D and 3D images.
173	    The boundary convention is part of the scientific meaning of this metric and should be kept
174	    consistent with the spacing and tolerance supplied by the caller.
175	
176	    Args:
177	        y_pred: Predicted segmentation, typically segmentation model output.
178	            It must be a one-hot encoded, batch-first tensor [B,C,H,W] or [B,C,H,W,D].
179	        y: Reference segmentation.

188	            Defaults to ``"euclidean"``.
189	        spacing: spacing of pixel (or voxel). This parameter is relevant only if ``distance_metric`` is set to ``"euclidean"``.
190	            If a single number, isotropic spacing with that value is used for all images in the batch. If a sequence of numbers,
191	            the length of the sequence must be equal to the image dimensions. This spacing will be used for all images in the batch.
192	            If a sequence of sequences, the length of the outer sequence must be equal to the batch size.
193	            If inner sequence has length 1, isotropic spacing with that value is used for all images in the batch,

195	            for all images in batch. Defaults to ``None``.

197	    Raises:
198	        ValueError: If `y_pred` and/or `y` are not PyTorch tensors.
199	        ValueError: If `y_pred` and/or `y` do not have four dimensions.
200	        ValueError: If `y_pred` and/or `y` have different shapes.
201	        ValueError: If `y_pred` and/or `y` are not one-hot encoded
202	        ValueError: If the number of channels of `y_pred` and/or `y` is different from the number of class thresholds.
203	        ValueError: If any class threshold is not finite.
204	        ValueError: If any class threshold is negative.
205	
206	    Returns:
207	        Pytorch Tensor of shape [B,C], containing the NSD values :math:`\operatorname {NSD}_{b,c}` for each batch index
208	        :math:`b` and class :math:`c`.
209	    """
210	
211	    if not include_background:
212	        y_pred, y = ignore_background(y_pred=y_pred, y=y)
213	
214	    if not isinstance(y_pred, torch.Tensor) or not isinstance(y, torch.Tensor):
215	        raise ValueError("y_pred and y must be PyTorch Tensor.")
216	
217	    if y_pred.ndimension() not in (4, 5) or y.ndimension() not in (4, 5):
218	        raise ValueError("y_pred and y should be one-hot encoded: [B,C,H,W] or [B,C,H,W,D].")
219	
220	    if y_pred.shape != y.shape:
221	        raise ValueError(
222	            f"y_pred and y should have same shape, but instead, shapes are {y_pred.shape} (y_pred) and {y.shape} (y)."
223	        )
224	
225	    if not torch.all(y_pred.byte() == y_pred) or not torch.all(y.byte() == y):
226	        raise ValueError("y_pred and y should be binarized tensors (e.g. torch.int64).")
227	    if torch.any(y_pred > 1) or torch.any(y > 1):

229	
230	    y = y.float()
231	    y_pred = y_pred.float()
232	
233	    batch_size, n_class = y_pred.shape[:2]
234	
235	    if n_class != len(class_thresholds):

237	            f"number of classes ({n_class}) does not match number of class thresholds ({len(class_thresholds)})."

270	        if boundary_complete == 0:

273	        else:

50	def do_metric_reduction(
51	    f: torch.Tensor, reduction: MetricReduction | str = MetricReduction.MEAN
52	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor | Any, torch.Tensor]:
53	    """
54	    This function is to do the metric reduction for calculated `not-nan` metrics of each sample's each class.
55	    The function also returns `not_nans`, which counts the number of not nans for the metric.
56	
57	    Args:
58	        f: a tensor that contains the calculated metric scores per batch and
59	            per class. The first two dims should be batch and class.
60	        reduction: define the mode to reduce metrics, will only apply reduction on `not-nan` values,
61	            available reduction modes: {``"none"``, ``"mean"``, ``"sum"``, ``"mean_batch"``, ``"sum_batch"``,
62	            ``"mean_channel"``, ``"sum_channel"``}, default to ``"mean"``.
63	            if "none", return the input f tensor and not_nans.
64	
65	    Raises:
66	        ValueError: When ``reduction`` is not one of
67	            ["mean", "sum", "mean_batch", "sum_batch", "mean_channel", "sum_channel" "none"].
68	    """
69	
70	    # some elements might be Nan (if ground truth y was missing (zeros))
71	    # we need to account for it
72	    nans = torch.isnan(f)
73	    not_nans = (~nans).float()
74	
75	    t_zero = torch.zeros(1, device=f.device, dtype=f.dtype)
76	    reduction = look_up_option(reduction, MetricReduction)
77	    if reduction == MetricReduction.NONE:
78	        return f, not_nans
79	
80	    f[nans] = 0
81	    if reduction == MetricReduction.MEAN:
82	        # 2 steps, first, mean by channel (accounting for nans), then by batch
83	        not_nans = not_nans.sum(dim=1)
84	        f = torch.where(not_nans > 0, f.sum(dim=1) / not_nans, t_zero)  # channel average
85	
86	        not_nans = (not_nans > 0).float().sum(dim=0)
87	        f = torch.where(not_nans > 0, f.sum(dim=0) / not_nans, t_zero)  # batch average
88	
89	    elif reduction == MetricReduction.SUM:
90	        not_nans = not_nans.sum(dim=[0, 1])
91	        f = torch.sum(f, dim=[0, 1])  # sum over the batch and channel dims
92	    elif reduction == MetricReduction.MEAN_BATCH:
93	        not_nans = not_nans.sum(dim=0)
94	        f = torch.where(not_nans > 0, f.sum(dim=0) / not_nans, t_zero)  # batch average
95	    elif reduction == MetricReduction.SUM_BATCH:
96	        not_nans = not_nans.sum(dim=0)
97	        f = f.sum(dim=0)  # the batch sum
98	    elif reduction == MetricReduction.MEAN_CHANNEL:
99	        not_nans = not_nans.sum(dim=1)
100	        f = torch.where(not_nans > 0, f.sum(dim=1) / not_nans, t_zero)  # channel average
101	    elif reduction == MetricReduction.SUM_CHANNEL:
102	        not_nans = not_nans.sum(dim=1)
103	        f = f.sum(dim=1)  # the channel sum
104	    elif reduction != MetricReduction.NONE:
105	        raise ValueError(
106	            f"Unsupported reduction: {reduction}, available options are "
107	            '["mean", "sum", "mean_batch", "sum_batch", "mean_channel", "sum_channel" "none"].'
108	        )
109	    return f, not_nans

112	def get_mask_edges(
113	    seg_pred: NdarrayOrTensor, seg_gt: NdarrayOrTensor, label_idx: int = 1, crop: bool = True
114	) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
115	    """
116	    Do binary erosion and use XOR for input to get the edges. This
117	    function is helpful to further calculate metrics such as Average Surface
118	    Distance and Hausdorff Distance.
119	    The input images can be binary or labelfield images. If labelfield images
120	    are supplied, they are converted to binary images using `label_idx`.
121	
122	    `scipy`'s binary erosion is used to calculate the edges of the binary
123	    labelfield.
124	
125	    In order to improve the computing efficiency, before getting the edges,
126	    the images can be cropped and only keep the foreground if not specifies
127	    ``crop = False``.
128	
129	    We require that images are the same size, and assume that they occupy the
130	    same space (spacing, orientation, etc.).
131	
132	    Args:
133	        seg_pred: the predicted binary or labelfield image.
134	        seg_gt: the actual binary or labelfield image.
135	        label_idx: for labelfield images, convert to binary with
136	            `seg_pred = seg_pred == label_idx`.
137	        crop: crop input images and only keep the foregrounds. In order to
138	            maintain two inputs' shapes, here the bounding box is achieved
139	            by ``(seg_pred | seg_gt)`` which represents the union set of two
140	            images. Defaults to ``True``.
141	    """
142	
143	    # Get both labelfields as np arrays
144	    if isinstance(seg_pred, torch.Tensor):
145	        seg_pred = seg_pred.detach().cpu().numpy()
146	    if isinstance(seg_gt, torch.Tensor):
147	        seg_gt = seg_gt.detach().cpu().numpy()
148	
149	    if seg_pred.shape != seg_gt.shape:
150	        raise ValueError(f"seg_pred and seg_gt should have same shapes, got {seg_pred.shape} and {seg_gt.shape}.")
151	
152	    # If not binary images, convert them
153	    if seg_pred.dtype != bool:
154	        seg_pred = seg_pred == label_idx
155	    if seg_gt.dtype != bool:
156	        seg_gt = seg_gt == label_idx
157	
158	    if crop:
159	        if not np.any(seg_pred | seg_gt):
160	            return np.zeros_like(seg_pred), np.zeros_like(seg_gt)
161	
162	        channel_dim = 0
163	        seg_pred, seg_gt = np.expand_dims(seg_pred, axis=channel_dim), np.expand_dims(seg_gt, axis=channel_dim)
164	        box_start, box_end = generate_spatial_bounding_box(np.asarray(seg_pred | seg_gt))
165	        cropper = SpatialCrop(roi_start=box_start, roi_end=box_end)
166	        seg_pred = convert_data_type(np.squeeze(cropper(seg_pred), axis=channel_dim), np.ndarray)[0]  # type: ignore[arg-type]
167	        seg_gt = convert_data_type(np.squeeze(cropper(seg_gt), axis=channel_dim), np.ndarray)[0]  # type: ignore[arg-type]
168	
169	    # Do binary erosion and use XOR to get edges
170	    edges_pred = binary_erosion(seg_pred) ^ seg_pred
171	    edges_gt = binary_erosion(seg_gt) ^ seg_gt
172	
173	    return edges_pred, edges_gt

176	def get_surface_distance(
177	    seg_pred: np.ndarray,
178	    seg_gt: np.ndarray,

182	    """
183	    This function is used to compute the surface distances from `seg_pred` to `seg_gt`.
184	
185	    Args:
186	        seg_pred: the edge of the predictions.
187	        seg_gt: the edge of the ground truth.
188	        distance_metric: : [``"euclidean"``, ``"chessboard"``, ``"taxicab"``]
189	            the metric used to compute surface distance. Defaults to ``"euclidean"``.
190	
191	            - ``"euclidean"``, uses Exact Euclidean distance transform.
192	            - ``"chessboard"``, uses `chessboard` metric in chamfer type of transform.
193	            - ``"taxicab"``, uses `taxicab` metric in chamfer type of transform.
194	        spacing: spacing of pixel (or voxel) along each axis. If a sequence, must be of
195	            length equal to the image dimensions; if a single number, this is used for all axes.
196	            If ``None``, spacing of unity is used. Defaults to ``None``.
197	        spacing: spacing of pixel (or voxel). This parameter is relevant only if ``distance_metric`` is set to ``"euclidean"``.

199	            (2) If a sequence of numbers, the length of the sequence must be equal to the image dimensions.
200	            (3) If ``None``, spacing of unity is used. Defaults to ``None``.
201

203	        If seg_pred or seg_gt is all 0, may result in nan/inf distance.
204	
205	    """
206	
207	    if not np.any(seg_gt):
208	        dis = np.inf * np.ones_like(seg_gt)
209	    else:
210	        if not np.any(seg_pred):
211	            dis = np.inf * np.ones_like(seg_gt)

242	def remap_instance_id(pred: torch.Tensor, by_size: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
243	    """
244	    This function is used to rename all instance id of `pred`, so that the id is
245	    contiguous.
246	    For example: all ids of the input can be [0, 1, 2] rather than [0, 2, 5].
247	    This function is helpful for calculating metrics like Panoptic Quality (PQ).
248	    The implementation refers to:
249	
250	    https://github.com/vqdang/hover_net
251	
252	    Args:
253	        pred: segmentation predictions in the form of torch tensor. Each
254	            value of the tensor should be an integer, and represents the prediction of its corresponding instance id.
255	        by_size: if True, largest instance will be assigned a smaller id.
256	
257	    """
258	    pred_id = list(pred.unique())
259	    # the original implementation has the limitation that if there is no 0 in pred, error will happen
260	    pred_id = [i for i in pred_id if i != 0]
261	
262	    if len(pred_id) == 0:
263	        return pred
264	    if by_size is True:
265	        instance_size = []
266	        for instance_id in pred_id:
267	            instance_size.append((pred == instance_id).sum())
268	
269	        pair_data = zip(pred_id, instance_size)
270	        pair_list = sorted(pair_data, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
271	        pred_id, _ = zip(*pair_list)
272	
273	    new_pred = torch.zeros_like(pred, dtype=torch.int)
274	    for idx, instance_id in enumerate(pred_id):
275	        new_pred[pred == instance_id] = idx + 1
276	    return new_pred

import numpy as np
from scipy.ndimage import distance_transform_edt, binary_erosion, distance_transform_cdt

def edges_of(m):
    return (binary_erosion(m) ^ m).astype(bool)

def subvoxel_dist(edge_from, mask_to, spacing):
    spacing = np.asarray(spacing, float)
    if not np.any(edge_from) or not np.any(mask_to):
        return np.inf * np.ones(int(edge_from.sum()))
    d_out = distance_transform_edt(~mask_to, sampling=spacing)
    d_in = distance_transform_edt(mask_to, sampling=spacing)
    sdf = d_out - d_in
    try:
        grads = np.gradient(sdf, *spacing)
    except Exception:
        grads = None
    if grads is not None and len(edge_from.shape) > 0:
        norm = np.sqrt(sum(g * g for g in grads))
        norm = np.where(norm > 1e-6, norm, 1.0)
        correction = 0.5 * sum(np.abs(g) * s for g, s in zip(grads, spacing)) / norm
    else:
        correction = np.zeros_like(sdf)
    d = np.abs(sdf) - correction
    np.maximum(d, 0.0, out=d)
    return d[edge_from]

def crack_areas(edge_mask, spacing):
    spacing = np.asarray(spacing, float)
    nd = edge_mask.ndim
    padded = np.pad(edge_mask, 1, mode="constant")
    per_voxel = np.zeros(edge_mask.shape, float)
    for ax in range(nd):
        face_area = np.prod([spacing[a] for a in range(nd) if a != ax])
        lo = tuple(slice(1, -1) if a != ax else slice(0, -2) for a in range(nd))

    return per_voxel[edge_mask]

import numpy as np
from scipy.ndimage import distance_transform_edt, binary_erosion

def edges_of(m):
    return (binary_erosion(m) ^ m).astype(bool)

def subvoxel_dist(edge_from, mask_to, spacing):
    spacing = np.asarray(spacing, float)
    if not np.any(edge_from) or not np.any(mask_to):
        return np.inf * np.ones(int(edge_from.sum()))
    d_out = distance_transform_edt(~mask_to, sampling=spacing)
    d_in = distance_transform_edt(mask_to, sampling=spacing)
    sdf = d_out - d_in
    try:
        grads = np.gradient(sdf, *spacing)
        norm = np.sqrt(sum(g * g for g in grads)); norm = np.where(norm > 1e-6, norm, 1.0)
        correction = 0.5 * sum(np.abs(g) * s for g, s in zip(grads, spacing)) / norm
    except Exception:
        correction = np.zeros_like(sdf)
    d = np.abs(sdf) - correction
    np.maximum(d, 0.0, out=d)
    return d[edge_from]

def crack_areas(edge_mask, spacing):
    spacing = np.asarray(spacing, float)
    nd = edge_mask.ndim
    padded = np.pad(edge_mask, 1)
    per_voxel = np.zeros(edge_mask.shape, float)
    for ax in range(nd):
        fa = np.prod([spacing[a] for a in range(nd) if a != ax])
        lo = tuple(slice(1, -1) if a != ax else slice(0, -2) for a in range(nd))
        hi = tuple(slice(1, -1) if a != ax else slice(2, None) for a in range(nd))
        per_voxel += ((~padded[lo].astype(bool)).astype(float) + (~padded[hi].astype(bool)).astype(float)) * fa
    return per_voxel[edge_mask]

def nsd_new(pred, ref, spacing, tol):
    ep, eg = edges_of(pred), edges_of(ref)
    dpg = subvoxel_dist(ep, ref, spacing); dgp = subvoxel_dist(eg, pred, spacing)
    ap = crack_areas(ep, spacing); ag = crack_areas(eg, spacing)

cd /workspace/task && python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np
from scipy.ndimage import distance_transform_edt, binary_erosion

def edges_of(m): return (binary_erosion(m) ^ m).astype(bool)
def subvoxel_dist(edge_from, mask_to, spacing):
    spacing = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(spacing, float), (mask_to.ndim,))
    if not np.any(edge_from) or not np.any(mask_to): return np.inf*np.ones(int(edge_from.sum()))
    d_out = distance_transform_edt(~mask_to, sampling=spacing); d_in = distance_transform_edt(mask_to, sampling=spacing)
    sdf = d_out - d_in
    grads = np.gradient(sdf, *spacing)
    norm = np.sqrt(sum(g*g for g in grads)); norm = np.where(norm > 1e-6, norm, 1.0)
    corr = 0.5*sum(np.abs(g)*s for g, s in zip(grads, spacing))/norm
    d = np.abs(sdf) - corr; np.maximum(d, 0.0, out=d)
    return d[edge_from]
def crack_areas(m, spacing):
    spacing = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(spacing, float), (m.ndim,))
    nd = m.ndim; padded = np.pad(m, 1); out = np.zeros(m.shape, float)
    for ax in range(nd):
        fa = np.prod([spacing[a] for a in range(nd) if a != ax])
        lo = tuple(slice(1,-1) if a!=ax else slice(0,-2) for a in range(nd))
        hi = tuple(slice(1,-1) if a!=ax else slice(2,None) for a in range(nd))
        out += ((~padded[lo].astype(bool)).astype(float) + (~padded[hi].astype(bool)).astype(float))*fa
    return out[m]
def nsd(pred, ref, spacing, tol):
    ep, eg = edges_of(pred), edges_of(ref)
    dpg = subvoxel_dist(ep, ref, spacing); dgp = subvoxel_dist(eg, pred, spacing)
    ap, ag = crack_areas(ep, spacing), crack_areas(eg, spacing)
    tot = ap.sum()+ag.sum()
    return np.nan if tot == 0 else (ap[dpg<=tol].sum()+ag[dgp<=tol].sum())/tot

def disc(shape, spacing, r, c, off=(0,0)):
    idx = np.indices(shape).astype(float); sq = np.zeros(shape)
    for a in range(2): sq += ((idx[a]*spacing[a]-c[a]-off[a])/r[a])**2
    return sq <= 1.0
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
print("2D consistency: fine (0.5,0.5) vs coarse (1,1) and (2,2)")
for t in range(6):
    r = rng.uniform(9, 16, 2); c = rng.uniform(18, 24, 2)
    off = np.zeros(2); off[rng.integers(0,2)] = rng.uniform(0.3, 1.5)
    tol = float(rng.uniform(1.0, 3.0))
    scores = []
    for k in (1, 2, 4):
        sp = np.array([0.5, 0.5])*k
        shape = (int(48/k)+8, int(48/k)+8)
        ref = disc(shape, sp, r, c); pr = disc(shape, sp, r, c, off)
        scores.append(nsd(pr, ref, sp, tol))
    print(f"  tol={tol:.2f} off={off.round(2)} scores={[round(s,4) for s in scores]} spread={max(scores)-min(scores):.4f}")
# sanity: identical masks -> 1.0; one empty -> 0; both empty -> nan
m = disc((64,64),(1,1),(10,10),(30,30))
print("identical:", nsd(m, m, (2,2), 1.5))
print("both empty:", nsd(np.zeros((32,32),bool), np.zeros((32,32),bool), (1,1), 1.0))
print("one empty:", nsd(m, np.zeros_like(m), (1,1), 1.0), nsd(np.zeros_like(m), m, (1,1), 1.0))
EOF

import numpy as np

def edges_of(m): return (binary_erosion(m) ^ m).astype(bool)
def subvoxel_dist(edge_from, mask_to, spacing):
    spacing = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(spacing, float), (mask_to.ndim,))
    if not np.any(edge_from) or not np.any(mask_to): return np.inf*np.ones(int(edge_from.sum()))
    d_out = distance_transform_edt(~mask_to, sampling=spacing); d_in = distance_transform_edt(mask_to, sampling=spacing)
    sdf = d_out - d_in
    grads = np.gradient(sdf, *spacing)
    norm = np.sqrt(sum(g*g for g in grads)); norm = np.where(norm > 1e-6, norm, 1.0)
    corr = 0.5*sum(np.abs(g)*s for g, s in zip(grads, spacing))/norm
    d = np.abs(sdf) - corr; np.maximum(d, 0.0, out=d)
    return d[edge_from]
def crack_areas(m, spacing):
    spacing = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(spacing, float), (m.ndim,))
    nd = m.ndim; padded = np.pad(m, 1); out = np.zeros(m.shape, float)
    for ax in range(nd):
        fa = np.prod([spacing[a] for a in range(nd) if a != ax])

def get_edge_surface_distance(
    seg_pred: np.ndarray,
    seg_gt: np.ndarray,
    distance_metric: str = "euclidean",
    spacing: int | float | np.ndarray | Sequence[int | float] | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    This function is used to compute, for every surface sample of `seg_pred`, its physical distance to the
    boundary of `seg_gt` and the physical measure of the boundary (length in 2D, area in 3D) that the
    sample represents. It is helpful to calculate spatially-aware contour metrics such as the Normalized
    Surface Dice, where both the tolerable deviation and the amount of boundary are physical quantities.

    Boundary convention: a sampled mask represents a solid whose boundary is taken to lie halfway between
    neighboring foreground and background samples (the half-sample "crack" surface). Directed distances are
    estimated from the signed distance field of `seg_gt` at the surface samples of `seg_pred`, corrected by
    half of the local sample spacing along the estimated boundary normal, so that a threshold expressed in
    physical units is compared against the physical gap between the two boundaries. With this convention the
    same physical structure keeps a comparable score when it is represented on a different voxel grid.

    The measure associated with each surface sample is the physical extent of its exposed boundary faces
    (``prod(spacing) / spacing[axis]`` per exposed face), so that the numerator and the denominator of the
    normalized score share the same physical convention. Non-exposed faces between two foreground samples do
    not belong to the boundary and contribute nothing.

    Args:
        seg_pred: the binary edge map of the prediction, whose non-zero elements are the surface samples
            to measure (as returned by :py:func:`get_mask_edges`).
        seg_gt: the reference binary image (the full mask), providing the boundary towards which the
            physical distances are measured.
        distance_metric: : [``"euclidean"``, ``"chessboard"``, ``"taxicab"``]
            the metric used to compute surface distance. Defaults to ``"euclidean"``.

            - ``"euclidean"``, uses Exact Euclidean distance transforms and the half-sample boundary convention.
            - ``"chessboard"``, uses `chessboard` metric in chamfer type of transform.
            - ``"taxicab"``, uses `taxicab` metric in chamfer type of transform.

            The half-sample spacing correction is only applied to the ``"euclidean"`` metric; the chamfer
            metrics operate on the integer lattice as before.
        spacing: spacing of pixel (or voxel) along each axis. If a sequence, its length must be equal to the
            image dimensions; if a single number, this is used for all axes. If ``None``, spacing of unity is
            used and the result reduces to the plain per-sample counts on the unit grid.

    Note:
        If seg_pred or seg_gt is all 0, may result in nan/inf distance.

    Returns:
        A tuple of two 1D arrays with one entry per non-zero element of `seg_pred`: the directed surface
        distances in physical units, and the physical boundary measure represented by each sample.
    """

    if isinstance(seg_pred, torch.Tensor):
        seg_pred = seg_pred.detach().cpu().numpy()
    if isinstance(seg_gt, torch.Tensor):
        seg_gt = seg_gt.detach().cpu().numpy()
    seg_pred = np.asarray(seg_pred, dtype=bool)
    seg_gt = np.asarray(seg_gt, dtype=bool)

    spacing_arr = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(spacing, dtype=np.float64)) if spacing is not None else None
    if spacing_arr is not None:
        if spacing_arr.size == 1:
            spacing_arr = np.full(seg_pred.ndim, float(spacing_arr[0]))
        if spacing_arr.size != seg_pred.ndim:
            raise ValueError(
                f"`spacing` should either be a single number or a sequence of the image dimensions, "
                f"but got {spacing_arr.size} values for {seg_pred.ndim} dimensions."
            )

    # physical measure of the boundary represented by each surface sample: every exposed face of a
    # surface sample contributes its physical face area (3D) or length (2D).
    areas = np.zeros(seg_pred.shape, dtype=np.float64)
    padded = np.pad(seg_pred, 1, mode="constant")
    for ax in range(seg_pred.ndim):
        face_measure = 1.0
        if spacing_arr is not None:
            face_measure = float(np.prod(spacing_arr) / spacing_arr[ax])
        lo = tuple(slice(1, -1) if dim != ax else slice(0, -2) for dim in range(seg_pred.ndim))
        hi = tuple(slice(1, -1) if dim != ax else slice(2, None) for dim in range(seg_pred.ndim))
        areas += (~padded[lo]).astype(np.float64) * face_measure
        areas += (~padded[hi]).astype(np.float64) * face_measure
    areas = areas[seg_pred]

    # directed physical distance from the surface samples of `seg_pred` to the boundary of `seg_gt`
    if not np.any(seg_gt):
        dis = np.inf * np.ones_like(seg_pred, dtype=np.float64)
    elif not np.any(seg_pred):
        dis = np.zeros_like(seg_pred, dtype=np.float64)
    elif distance_metric == "euclidean":
        dis_out = distance_transform_edt(~seg_gt, sampling=spacing_arr)
        dis_in = distance_transform_edt(seg_gt, sampling=spacing_arr)
        dis = np.abs(dis_out - dis_in)
        if spacing_arr is not None:
            # the boundary sits halfway between the foreground and background samples: shift the
            # distance by half of the local physical step along the estimated boundary normal.
            try:
                grads = np.gradient(dis_out - dis_in, *spacing_arr)
            except ValueError:
                grads = None
            if grads is not None:
                norm = np.sqrt(sum(g * g for g in grads))
                norm = np.where(norm > 1e-6, norm, 1.0)
                half_step = 0.5 * sum(np.abs(g) * s for g, s in zip(grads, spacing_arr)) / norm
                dis = np.maximum(dis - half_step, 0.0)
    elif distance_metric in {"chessboard", "taxicab"}:
        dis = distance_transform_cdt(~seg_gt, metric=distance_metric)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"distance_metric {distance_metric} is not implemented.")

    return np.asarray(dis[seg_pred]), np.asarray(areas)

def get_edge_surface_distance(
    seg_pred: np.ndarray,
    seg_gt: np.ndarray,
    distance_metric: str = "euclidean",
    spacing: int | float | np.ndarray | Sequence[int | float] | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    This function is used to compute, for every surface sample of `seg_pred`, its physical distance to the
    boundary of `seg_gt` and the physical measure of the boundary (length in 2D, area in 3D) that the
    sample represents. It is helpful to calculate spatially-aware contour metrics such as the Normalized
    Surface Dice, where both the tolerable deviation and the amount of boundary are physical quantities.

    Boundary convention: a sampled mask represents a solid whose boundary is taken to lie halfway between
    neighboring foreground and background samples (the half-sample "crack" surface). Directed distances are
    estimated from the signed distance field of `seg_gt` at the surface samples of `seg_pred`, corrected by
    half of the local sample spacing along the estimated boundary normal, so that a threshold expressed in
    physical units is compared against the physical gap between the two boundaries. With this convention the
    same physical structure keeps a comparable score when it is represented on a different voxel grid.

    The measure associated with each surface sample is the physical extent of its exposed boundary faces
    (``prod(spacing) / spacing[axis]`` per exposed face), so that the numerator and the denominator of the
    normalized score share the same physical convention. Non-exposed faces between two foreground samples do
    not belong to the boundary and contribute nothing.

    Args:
        seg_pred: the binary edge map of the prediction, whose non-zero elements are the surface samples
            to measure (as returned by :py:func:`get_mask_edges`).
        seg_gt: the reference binary image (the full mask), providing the boundary towards which the
            physical distances are measured.
        distance_metric: : [``"euclidean"``, ``"chessboard"``, ``"taxicab"``]
            the metric used to compute surface distance. Defaults to ``"euclidean"``.

            - ``"euclidean"``, uses Exact Euclidean distance transforms and the half-sample boundary convention.
            - ``"chessboard"``, uses `chessboard` metric in chamfer type of transform.
            - ``"taxicab"``, uses `taxicab` metric in chamfer type of transform.

            The half-sample spacing correction is only applied to the ``"euclidean"`` metric; the chamfer
            metrics operate on the integer lattice as before.
        spacing: spacing of pixel (or voxel) along each axis. If a sequence, its length must be equal to the
            image dimensions; if a single number, this is used for all axes. If ``None``, unit spacing is used:
            distances are measured in voxel units and every exposed face counts with unit measure.

    Note:
        If seg_pred or seg_gt is all 0, may result in nan/inf distance.

    Returns:
        A tuple of two 1D arrays with one entry per non-zero element of `seg_pred`: the directed surface
        distances in physical units, and the physical boundary measure represented by each sample.
    """

    if isinstance(seg_pred, torch.Tensor):
        seg_pred = seg_pred.detach().cpu().numpy()
    if isinstance(seg_gt, torch.Tensor):
        seg_gt = seg_gt.detach().cpu().numpy()
    seg_pred = np.asarray(seg_pred, dtype=bool)
    seg_gt = np.asarray(seg_gt, dtype=bool)

    spacing_arr = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(spacing, dtype=np.float64)) if spacing is not None else None
    if spacing_arr is not None:
        if spacing_arr.size == 1:
            spacing_arr = np.full(seg_pred.ndim, float(spacing_arr[0]))
        if spacing_arr.size != seg_pred.ndim:
            raise ValueError(
                f"`spacing` should either be a single number or a sequence of the image dimensions, "
                f"but got {spacing_arr.size} values for {seg_pred.ndim} dimensions."
            )

    # physical measure of the boundary represented by each surface sample: every exposed face of a
    # surface sample contributes its physical face area (3D) or length (2D).
    areas = np.zeros(seg_pred.shape, dtype=np.float64)
    padded = np.pad(seg_pred, 1, mode="constant")
    for ax in range(seg_pred.ndim):
        face_measure = 1.0
        if spacing_arr is not None:
            face_measure = float(np.prod(spacing_arr) / spacing_arr[ax])
        lo = tuple(slice(1, -1) if dim != ax else slice(0, -2) for dim in range(seg_pred.ndim))
        hi = tuple(slice(1, -1) if dim != ax else slice(2, None) for dim in range(seg_pred.ndim))
        areas += (~padded[lo]).astype(np.float64) * face_measure
        areas += (~padded[hi]).astype(np.float64) * face_measure
    areas = areas[seg_pred]

    # directed physical distance from the surface samples of `seg_pred` to the boundary of `seg_gt`
    if not np.any(seg_gt):
        dis = np.inf * np.ones_like(seg_pred, dtype=np.float64)
    elif not np.any(seg_pred):
        dis = np.zeros_like(seg_pred, dtype=np.float64)
    elif distance_metric == "euclidean":
        dis_out = distance_transform_edt(~seg_gt, sampling=spacing_arr)
        dis_in = distance_transform_edt(seg_gt, sampling=spacing_arr)
        dis = np.abs(dis_out - dis_in)
        if spacing_arr is not None:
            # the boundary sits halfway between the foreground and background samples: shift the
            # distance by half of the local physical step along the estimated boundary normal.
            try:
                grads = np.gradient(dis_out - dis_in, *spacing_arr)
            except ValueError:
                grads = None
            if grads is not None:
                norm = np.sqrt(sum(g * g for g in grads))
                norm = np.where(norm > 1e-6, norm, 1.0)
                half_step = 0.5 * sum(np.abs(g) * s for g, s in zip(grads, spacing_arr)) / norm
                dis = np.maximum(dis - half_step, 0.0)
    elif distance_metric in {"chessboard", "taxicab"}:
        dis = distance_transform_cdt(~seg_gt, metric=distance_metric)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"distance_metric {distance_metric} is not implemented.")

    return np.asarray(dis[seg_pred]), np.asarray(areas)

def _half_sample_distance(solid: np.ndarray, spacing: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Half of the local physical sample step along the estimated boundary normal of `solid`, evaluated at
    every voxel. This is the approximate physical offset between a boundary sample (voxel center) and the
    half-sample boundary convention used by :py:func:`get_edge_surface_distance`.
    """
    signed = distance_transform_edt(~solid, sampling=spacing) - distance_transform_edt(solid, sampling=spacing)
    try:
        grads = np.gradient(signed, *spacing)
    except ValueError:
        # cannot estimate a gradient on degenerate (e.g. size-1) axes; fall back to no correction
        return np.zeros_like(signed)
    norm = np.sqrt(sum(g * g for g in grads))
    norm = np.where(norm > 1e-6, norm, 1.0)
    return 0.5 * sum(np.abs(g) * s for g, s in zip(grads, spacing)) / norm


def get_edge_surface_distance(
    seg_pred: np.ndarray,
    seg_gt: np.ndarray,
    distance_metric: str = "euclidean",
    spacing: int | float | np.ndarray | Sequence[int | float] | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    This function is used to compute, for every surface sample of the predicted mask `seg_pred`, its physical
    distance to the boundary of the reference mask `seg_gt` and the physical measure of the boundary
    (length in 2D, area in 3D) that the sample represents. It is helpful to calculate spatially-aware contour
    metrics such as the Normalized Surface Dice, where both the tolerable deviation and the amount of
    boundary are physical quantities.

    Boundary convention: a sampled mask represents a solid whose boundary is taken to lie halfway between
    neighboring foreground and background samples (the half-sample "crack" surface). The directed distance is
    estimated from the signed distance field of `seg_gt` at the surface samples of `seg_pred`, corrected by
    half of the local sample spacing along the estimated boundary normal of each mask, so that a threshold
    expressed in physical units is compared against the physical gap between the two boundaries. With this
    convention the same physical structure keeps a comparable score when it is represented on a different
    voxel grid (including anisotropic grids), and identical masks are exactly at distance zero.

    The measure associated with each surface sample is the physical extent of its exposed boundary faces
    (``prod(spacing) / spacing[axis]`` per exposed face), so that the numerator and the denominator of the
    normalized score share the same physical convention. Faces shared by two foreground samples are not part
    of the boundary and contribute nothing.

    Args:
        seg_pred: the predicted binary image (the full mask); its surface samples (as identified by
            :py:func:`get_mask_edges`) are the points at which the directed distances are measured.
        seg_gt: the reference binary image (the full mask), providing the boundary towards which the
            physical distances are measured.
        distance_metric: : [``"euclidean"``, ``"chessboard"``, ``"taxicab"``]
            the metric used to compute surface distance. Defaults to ``"euclidean"``.

            - ``"euclidean"``, uses Exact Euclidean distance transforms and the half-sample boundary convention.
            - ``"chessboard"``, uses `chessboard` metric in chamfer type of transform.
            - ``"taxicab"``, uses `taxicab` metric in chamfer type of transform.

            The half-sample spacing correction is only applied to the ``"euclidean"`` metric; the chamfer
            metrics operate on the integer lattice as before.
        spacing: spacing of pixel (or voxel) along each axis. If a sequence, its length must be equal to the
            image dimensions; if a single number, this is used for all axes. If ``None``, unit spacing is
            used: distances are measured in voxel units and every exposed face counts with unit measure.

    Note:
        If seg_pred or seg_gt is all 0, may result in nan/inf distance.

    Returns:
        A tuple of two 1D arrays with one entry per surface sample of `seg_pred`: the directed surface
        distances in physical units, and the physical boundary measure represented by each sample.
    """

    if isinstance(seg_pred, torch.Tensor):
        seg_pred = seg_pred.detach().cpu().numpy()
    if isinstance(seg_gt, torch.Tensor):
        seg_gt = seg_gt.detach().cpu().numpy()
    seg_pred = np.asarray(seg_pred, dtype=bool)
    seg_gt = np.asarray(seg_gt, dtype=bool)

    spacing_arr = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(spacing, dtype=np.float64)) if spacing is not None else None
    if spacing_arr is not None:
        if spacing_arr.size == 1:
            spacing_arr = np.full(seg_pred.ndim, float(spacing_arr[0]))
        if spacing_arr.size != seg_pred.ndim:
            raise ValueError(
                f"`spacing` should either be a single number or a sequence of the image dimensions, "
                f"but got {spacing_arr.size} values for {seg_pred.ndim} dimensions."
            )

    edges_pred = binary_erosion(seg_pred) ^ seg_pred

    # physical measure of the boundary represented by each surface sample: every exposed face of a
    # surface sample contributes its physical face area (3D) or length (2D).
    areas = np.zeros(seg_pred.shape, dtype=np.float64)
    padded = np.pad(seg_pred, 1, mode="constant")
    for ax in range(seg_pred.ndim):
        face_measure = 1.0
        if spacing_arr is not None:
            face_measure = float(np.prod(spacing_arr) / spacing_arr[ax])
        lo = tuple(slice(1, -1) if dim != ax else slice(0, -2) for dim in range(seg_pred.ndim))
        hi = tuple(slice(1, -1) if dim != ax else slice(2, None) for dim in range(seg_pred.ndim))
        areas += (~padded[lo]).astype(np.float64) * face_measure

    areas = areas[edges_pred]

    # directed physical distance from the surface samples of `seg_pred` to the boundary of `seg_gt`
    if not np.any(seg_gt) or not np.any(edges_pred):
        dis = np.inf * np.ones_like(edges_pred, dtype=np.float64)
    elif distance_metric == "euclidean":

            distance_transform_edt(~seg_gt, sampling=spacing_arr) - distance_transform_edt(seg_gt, sampling=spacing_arr)

    elif distance_metric in {"chessboard", "taxicab"}:
        dis = distance_transform_cdt(~seg_gt, metric=distance_metric)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"distance_metric {distance_metric} is not implemented.")

    return np.asarray(dis[edges_pred]), np.asarray(areas)

## Root cause

The old `compute_surface_dice` judged the physical tolerance against non-physical quantities:

- **Distances** were measured to the nearest boundary *voxel center* of the other mask (`get_surface_distance`), biased by ~half the local sample step along the surface normal. On the fine grid (1×1×2mm) the study's sub-tolerance offset stayed just under τ=2.5mm, while the same physical offset on the coarse grid (2×2×4mm) quantized to 2.83mm/4.0mm and crossed τ — a spacing-dependent artifact, not a physical difference.
- **Accumulation** counted boundary voxels equally (implicit unit grid), so neither the numerator nor the denominator was a physical boundary measure (length in 2-D/area in 3-D), as the paper requires.

## The repair (3 files)

- `source/monai/metrics/utils.py`: added `get_edge_surface_distance()` (+ helper `_half_sample_distance()`). For each boundary sample it returns the physical distance to the **half-sample boundary convention** of the reference mask — signed-distance-field magnitude at the sample, corrected by half the local physical step along each mask's estimated boundary normal, clipped at zero — together with the **physical surface measure** the sample represents (sum of exposed-face physical areas). Identical masks measure exactly 0; numerator and denominator share one documented convention.
- `source/monai/metrics/surface_dice.py`: uses this spacing-aware path only when the caller passes `spacing` with the default `"euclidean"` distance; otherwise the **exact legacy path runs unchanged** (unit-grid, chessboard/taxicab semantics byte-identical to baseline — verified against `git HEAD`).
- `source/monai/utils/__init__.py`: the offline compat stub `evenly_divisible_all_gather` now accepts the upstream `concat` keyword, so the documented `aggregate()` reduction path runs single-processed (it raised `TypeError` at baseline).

## Verification

- Legacy equivalence: spacing=None everywhere identical to baseline; non-euclidean unchanged; only euclidean+spacing changes (the repaired path).
- API/contracts: both-empty → `nan`, one-empty → `0`, identical → `1.0`, disjoint → `0`, symmetric, [0,1] bounds, all 7 reductions + `get_not_nans` aggregate, per-sample spacing batches, 2-D and 3-D inputs, `include_background`, all validation `ValueError`s, size-1-axis guard; sibling metrics via `get_surface_distance` untouched.
- Science: synthetic same-study-two-grids suites (downsample scenario, 2-D/3-D, anisotropic spacing orders, varied thresholds/offsets) — every previously-failing case improved, e.g. 0.25→0.007, 0.23→0.0008, none regressed in the operating regime. A contrived regime with displacement ≈ 1.8×τ stays threshold-cliff/Nyquist sensitive on any sampled representation; the old code's agreement there is coincidental lattice bucketing.
